did.abstract: Three letters (with envelopes) and one telegram addressed to members of the Bottitta family of Brooklyn.

arrangement.head: Arrangement
arrangement.p: This small collection is housed in a single folder with the items arranged chronologically.

bioghist.head: Biographical note
bioghist.p: The Bottitta family was headed by father Charles (born circa 1884) and mother Silvestra (born circa 1889), who were both born in Italy and immigrated to the United States around 1900. They settled in Brooklyn and raised several children, including Ann (born 1911 or 1912), Vito (born circa 1910), Mary (born circa 1908), and Charles (born circa 1923). In the 1920 census, the family was living at 398 Watkins Street in Brownsville. In 1930, they were living at 41 Sumner Avenue (now Marcus Garvey Boulevard) in Bushwick. In both the 1940 and 1950 censuses, the family was living at 161 Suydam Street, on the corner of Central Avenue, also in Bushwick. In 1948, Mary married Paul Rodolico, whose family is listed as also living at 161 Suydam Street in the 1950 census.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: Three letters (with envelopes) and one telegram addressed to members of the Bottitta family of Brooklyn.

The telegram, dated April 1945, is from the US government regarding Vito Bottitta having been "slightly wounded" while serving in Germany. It is addressed to Charles Bottitta at 161 Central Avenue, Brooklyn.

The letters are all addressed to Ann Bottitta from Mary and Paul Rodolico of San Diego. The first is c/o Bernard Workman of Manhattan, the second c/o Lo Murno of 996 Willoughby Avenue, and the third to 161 Central Avenue. All three letters are regarding Mary's pregnancy, childbirth, and the wellbeing of her daughter, with some mentions of other family members, as well as Mary's desire to move back to New York.
